title: Inequality chain bounding the failure probability of the CVM estimate
intent: Reduce the main CVM correctness theorem — that the probability the estimate returned by cvm is wrong is at most δ — to five named lemmas: one discharges the trivial empty-list / oversized-threshold case exactly, and the other four supply the three links of a single 'also … finally' chain that bounds the failure probability, the k > l error and the k ≤ l out-of-range error, whose bounds sum to δ.

children.name: prob_run_steps_is_None_or_pred_le
children.statement:
theorem prob_run_steps_is_None_or_pred_le : \\

(state in run_steps xs initial_state. state |> is_None_or_pred P) \ real (length xs) * f ^ threshold + \

(state in run_steps_no_fail xs initial_state. P state)\ (is \?L is_None_or_pred \ ?R\)
children.closed_by: smt (verit, del_insts) combining prob_fail_run_steps_le and prob_measure_spmf_le_of_ord_spmf[OF run_steps_le_run_steps_no_fail]
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the probability that run_steps fails or gives a wrong result is bounded by the fail probability plus the no-fail wrong-result probability, generically in P

children.name: run_steps_no_fail_eq_run_steps_eager_bernoulli_matrix
children.statement:
corollary run_steps_no_fail_eq_run_steps_eager_bernoulli_matrix :
  assumes "length xs \<le> n"
  shows
    "run_steps_no_fail xs initial_state = (
      bernoulli_matrix n n f
        |> map_pmf (run_reader <| run_steps_eager xs initial_state))"
children.closed_by: using run_steps_no_fail_eq_lazy sample_run_steps_eager_eq_run_steps_lazy by (metis bernoulli_matrix_def local.space_def sample_def)
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: run_steps_no_fail equals the eager algorithm run over a Bernoulli random matrix

applicability.goal_shape: An upper bound Pr[event] <= delta whose event is a disjunction ('the algorithm fails' OR 'the algorithm returns a wrong estimate'), proved as an ordered <= chain from the left-hand probability to a sum of named error bounds that the assumptions already cap at delta.
applicability.use_when: each link of the chain is non-trivial enough to deserve its own named lemma, and the links are ordered in one direction (< / <= / =) so Isar's 'also' composes them; the trivial cases (empty input, oversized threshold) can be split off first and closed exactly.
applicability.avoid_when: the links are one-off rewrites with no reuse (fold them inline); the chain needs >= steps, which Isar's 'also' does not compose by default; a single library theorem closes the whole bound; the case split's trivial branch needs the same machinery as the general branch.

consequences: The move creates one obligation per link: each named lemma must be proved in its own right before 'also ... finally' composes them. Transitivity of the chain is automatic. A link stated too weak breaks the final result; here the last step needs prob_fail_bound + prob_k_gt_l_bound + prob_k_le_l_and_est_out_of_range_bound <= delta, which the assumptions package as a single hypothesis discharged by 'unfolding prob_bounds_defs'. The two error-bound children carry their own Chernoff and geometric-series sub-chains, so the decomposition's weight lies in the leaves, not in the 40-line glue.
